A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Block-Attention research. All nine pages of v1 and twelve pages of v4, including equations, figures, tables and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-benchmark accuracy results, checkpoint evaluations, and latency/FLOP measurements in Tables 1–2 and Figure 4.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and efficiency results and adds position-re-encoding ablations and further accuracy summaries.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.5 retain the same independent-block attention mask, passage segmentation, RoPE position adjustment, block fine-tuning and cached inference procedure. The new experiments disable an existing component; they do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on TriviaQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA and evaluate on those datasets plus Natural Questions and HotpotQA. The cached-passage efficiency scenarios are retained. Code generation and dialogue remain suggested applications rather than evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The vanilla and block-without-fine-tuning baselines persist under revised names. v4 adds fine-tuned models without position re-encoding for both backbones. Section 3.3 also reports a Prompt Cache reimplementation matching the weak-baseline rows and a qualitative PCW comparison below those baselines, without separate PCW scores.

E3.justification: v4 introduces the control that disables position re-encoding. Its reported training setup also changes from explicit Flash-Attention V2 for SFT and SDPA for block training to a general Flash-Attention V2 description; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Model sizes, optimization hyperparameters, answer-matching accuracy and the 200-token output limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's fine-tuning comparison and checkpoint analysis, v4 tests the contribution of another central method component: position re-encoding. Table 1 ablates it across both backbones and all four benchmarks, reporting mixed-average losses of 4.5 points for Llama3 and 3.5 for Mistral. This supplies previously absent component-level validation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v4's added domain averages summarize benchmark accuracy, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds complete position-ablation results and in-/out-domain averages. Mistral-block's TQA/2Wiki/NQ/HQA scores change from 70.7/69.0/50.5/58.6 to 69.9/70.5/50.8/57.9, and its aggregate changes from 62.8 to 62.3. Llama3's weak-baseline 2Wiki and NQ scores change from 42.1 and 43.2 to 48.1 and 43.3. Figure 4 adds zero-step points while retaining the subsequent trajectories. These materially expand and revise reported evidence; Table 2's latency and FLOP values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The sequence/KV definitions and three RoPE equations are retained with equivalent mathematical content. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that blockwise KV reuse with fine-tuning preserves RAG accuracy while sharply reducing first-token latency and computation. v4 foregrounds computational cost in its title and abstract, but FLOP savings were already claimed in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 newly interprets the position ablation as evidence that re-encoding is essential. It also argues that Prompt Cache's position dependence restricts reuse when passage rankings change. The existing passage-interference conjecture, exclusion of cache costs and discussion of broader applications remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 removes v1's project-code availability footnote, adds a DeepSpeed access link, explicitly identifies Flash-Attention for inference, and revises the training-backend description. Hardware and numerical hyperparameters are retained. Removal of the code-link disclosure does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v1 lacks a dedicated related-work discussion. v4 adds Section 4 covering RAG and inference efficiency, substantially expanding citations and positioning against FiD, PCW, Prompt Cache and RAGCache. It explicitly distinguishes architecture compatibility, context-window objectives and position-dependent cache reuse.

P1.justification: The title changes from Low-Latency RAG to Efficient RAG, and the abstract and selected introductory and experimental passages are rewritten. Experimental setup paragraphs become numbered subsections, training and evaluation descriptions are separated, and related work is inserted. Much of the method and discussion wording remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains ablation rows, domain-average columns and stronger visual emphasis. Figure 3 adds explicit document/query divisions, Figure 2 updates terminology, and Figure 4 expands its vertical range for the added zero-step points. Table 2 relabels its first prompt-length column from 0 to 50. The same four figures and two tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The new position ablation supplies useful evidence absent from v1: disabling re-encoding reduces accuracy on every benchmark for both models. Section 4 also improves research positioning. These gains are tempered by reporting defects: v4's abstract retains 62.8 while Table 1 reports 62.3 for Mistral, and its Llama3-vanilla in-domain average of 73.9 exceeds both constituent scores, 72.8 and 73.4. Together with removal of the project-code link, these problems limit the overall improvement.
